prerequisites: EM1012 - Mecánica de Máquinas y Estructuras
EM1015 - Ciencia y Tecnología de Materiales
EM1019 - Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales
EM1020 - Teoría de Máquinas y Mecanismos

learning_outcomes.text: Be able to elaborate on teamwork in the field of manufacturing engineering through experimentation.
Be able to analyze and solve specific technological and economic problems in the field of manufacturing.
Be able to analyze the differences in metal part forming, considering technological and economic aspects.
Be able to explain, compare, and differentiate the different manufacturing processes and technologies.
Be able to explain, compare, and differentiate the different inspection processes.
Be able to apply different metrological and quality control techniques.
Know the current regulations related to the field of manufacturing processes.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: DIMENSIONAL AND GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES.
BLOCK II: SHAPING PROCESSES WITHOUT CHIP REMOVAL
Topic 9. Fundamentals of sheet metal working. Processes.
BLOCK III: SHAPING PROCESSES WITH CHIP REMOVAL
Topic 19. Metal coating and deposition processes.
Laboratory 1: Knowledge and handling of measurement equipment and instruments. Calibration of a measurement instrument.
Laboratory 2: Verification of dimensional and geometric characteristics of a part.
Laboratory 3: Forming of metallic parts by molding and plastic deformation.
Laboratory 4: Forming by chip removal: filing, slotting, and turning.
Laboratory 5: Forming by chip removal: milling, hole machining, and threading.
teaching_methods: Lecture: Used in theoretical classes to transmit structured knowledge on manufacturing technologies.
Exercise and Problem Solving: Used in practical problem-solving classes for calculating technical parameters in specific application cases of part forming technologies.

Laboratory Work: Used in practical laboratory classes for learning the handling and application range of inspection and measurement instruments, and for exposure to the reality of some part forming processes (machines, tooling, tools, etc.).
Project-Based Learning: Applied in practical classes (problems and laboratory) for designing complete processes for part verification and manufacturing based on quality and production requirements.
assessment_rules: To pass, an overall average grade of at least 5 out of 10 is required. For the first call, the final exam (60%) necessitates a minimum of 3.5 points in both theoretical and problem-solving sections; otherwise, the exam grade is capped at 4 points, and the overall module grade cannot exceed 4 if any minimums are not met. Continuous assessment includes non-recoverable lab practicals (10%) and group lab work (10%), plus a written test (20%) recoverable during the second recovery period's final exam. The second call's final exam is 80% (incorporating the written test), with 20% from continuous assessment, and a special degree completion session has a 100% final exam with similar minimum conditions.
